originalTitle: Bill Miller's investing strategy: How the legendary fund manager outperformed the market for 15 straight years
simplifiedContent: Bill Miller is a well-known investor who was able to do better than the overall stock market for 15 years in a row. He achieved this by using a strategy that combines finding undervalued companies, being patient, and going against the crowd. Miller looks for companies with strong finances and a "margin of safety", which means they are unlikely to lose a lot of value. He holds onto these companies until they reach a price that reflects their true worth or until his reasons for investing in them change. This approach helped Miller outperform the market, making him a successful and respected investor.

originalTitle: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank posts Rs 34 crore Q1 loss; asset quality stress persists
simplifiedContent: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank recently announced that it lost Rs 34 crore in the first quarter of the year. This is the fifth quarter in a row that the bank has reported a loss. The bank's poor performance is largely due to the fact that many of its loans are not being paid back on time, which is known as "asset quality stress". Although the bank's loss is smaller than it was in previous quarters, it still has a significant number of bad loans, making up 6.1% of its total loans. This news matters because it shows that the bank is still struggling to manage its loans and turn a profit.

originalTitle: Muthoot Finance reports 25% rise in Q1 profit, announces leadership transition
simplifiedContent: Muthoot Finance, a company that lends money to people using their gold as security, made a profit of Rs 2,550 crore in the first quarter of the year. This is 25% more than what they made during the same time last year. The main reason for this increase in profit is that their gold loan business is doing very well. The company is also making some changes in its leadership, with Alexander George Muthoot set to become the new managing director. This change will happen on October 1, if the company's shareholders agree to it.

originalTitle: Week Ahead: Wall Street eyes US jobs data, SpaceX debut earnings and Disney results
simplifiedContent: This week, investors are waiting to see how many new jobs were created in the US in July. This information is important because it will help them understand what might happen to interest rates in the coming months. Interest rates affect how much it costs to borrow money, which can impact the stock market. Investors will be paying close attention to this report to see what it might mean for their investments. The jobs report is considered the most important economic news of the week, and it will influence the decisions of investors on Wall Street.

originalTitle: Sebi order against Zee likely to delay planned  ₹3,143-crore fundraise
simplifiedContent: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has made an order against Zee that will likely delay their plan to raise ₹3,143 crore. This is because Sebi has stopped Zee from participating in the securities market for a while. As a result, Zee won't be able to buy or sell securities, which means their fundraising plan will probably be put on hold. This matters because Zee was counting on raising this money, and the delay could affect their plans. The order is a significant development for Zee and may impact their future activities.

originalTitle: Yen Traders Brace for More Intervention With US at Japan’s Side
simplifiedContent: Some big investors who deal with the Japanese yen are getting ready for Japan and the US to work together again to affect the value of the yen. This is because they did something similar last week in Tokyo and New York, and it caused the yen's value to go up quickly. This "intervention" is when countries intentionally try to change the value of their currency. It matters because it can affect how much money investors make or lose when they buy or sell the yen. As a result, these investors are paying close attention to what might happen on Monday when Asian markets open.
